# Avoid fork-only symbols in code compiled by stock Flutter

## Platform difference

A runtime platform guard cannot make an unknown fork-only Dart symbol compile under stock Flutter.

## Implementation

PiliPlus replaces an OH-only TargetPlatform enum reference with its OS abstraction in shared editable-text code. NipaPlay switches Platform.isOhos checks to operatingSystem string checks and provides a helper that copies its OH override file into the active pubspec_overrides.yaml. Nomark keeps its app-owned OH bridge in the native runner; this is a different packaging choice, not proof that stock Flutter builds OH.

## Applicability

Useful when a repository intentionally supports both stock Flutter development/CI and a Flutter OH build. Platform-specific imports and dependency APIs still require review, including web builds where dart:io cannot be imported unconditionally.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

pubspec_overrides.ohos.yaml is a project convention activated by a script, not automatic OS-specific pub resolution. A successfully analyzed common library does not certify OH toolchain support.

## Verification

Run the appropriate analyzer for each supported SDK and verify which override file is actually active in developer and CI environments.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
